title: Cancel or document the leaked DNS-lookup Future in ConnectivityGateway.isOnline on timeout
rule: Nygard lens — what happens when I/O fails halfway
why: Future.timeout() races a Timer against the lookup but cannot cancel the underlying OS-level DNS resolution — dart:io gives no cancellable primitive for InternetAddress.lookup. Under packet loss or a captive portal (exactly when this check matters most), the original lookup keeps running past the 2s timeout with no way to observe or cancel it; repeated calls (e.g. retrying a failed offline-account conversion in account_actions.dart) can accumulate abandoned lookups.
recommendation: Either document the accepted tradeoff inline (dart:io has no cancellable DNS API) with a bounded-impact justification, or switch to a primitive that supports cancellation (e.g. a raw socket connect with explicit close on timeout).
acceptance_criteria: Either an inline comment documents the accepted leak and its bound, or a test demonstrates no more than one lookup stays in flight after repeated rapid isOnline calls under a simulated timeout

corrections: account_actions.dart:226's isOnline call is inside showDeleteAccountFlow (delete-account-requires-internet), not an offline-account-conversion retry path; the core evidence at connectivity_gateway.dart:14 is unaffected.
